posts.title: The Download: AI’s trillion-dollar gamble and OpenAI’s biology data bid
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble When Jessica Wachter, a finance professor at the University of Pennsylvania, wanted to assess AI’s impact on the economy over the next few years,…
bullets: Financial analysis suggests that hyperscalers investing in AI infrastructure will face a $1.1 trillion expenditure by 2027, requiring massive productivity gains by 2030 to justify the capital outlay.
OpenAI is launching an initiative to acquire and curate 'biotech’s lost archive' by purchasing proprietary data from bankrupt biotech firms to train more capable medical AI models.
The strategy to monetize failed biotech regulatory filings and manufacturing data represents a new frontier in the 'data war' for specialized, high-quality training sets.
Despite growing concerns over existential risks, major industry leaders including Nvidia and Meta have explicitly rejected calls for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

posts.title: China NEV retail sales fall 10% in first 13 days of September, penetration at 70.3%
posts.summary:
China's passenger NEV retail sales totaled 362,000 in September 1-13, up 16% from the same period last month but down 10% from a year earlier.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's passenger NEV retail sales reached 362,000 units in the first 13 days of September, representing a 10% year-on-year decline.
NEV retail penetration hit 70.3%, driven by a continued slump in traditional gasoline vehicle sales.
Wholesale NEV sales showed resilience with a 1% year-on-year increase, supported by strong export performance.
Automakers are increasingly prioritizing volume targets to maintain production levels, leading to high penetration rates despite the lack of strong order backlogs.

The challenge is moving all of that data through the system without slowing down the testing processes.

Robotics is entering a new era.
Foundation models, vision-language-action systems, world models, and generative AI are transforming what robots can perceive, reason about, and do.
In this white paper, Federico Pecora, Senior Principal Robotics Research Lead at Arm, explores the systems-level challenges shaping the future of robotics.
The paper examines the architectural challenges that must be solved to enable the next generation of intelligent, trustworthy, and scalable physical AI systems.
